host.binding: numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 (all 48 CPUs of the single NUMA node), so 8 workers have 48 CPUs

command: dive-bench --set <shard-set.toml> --dive-bin ~/bins/dive --dive-revision 08a14fbac83ff71a3247623fb10bf0584bc83be5 --profile default --workers 1,4,8 --reps 3 --timeout 3600 --xmx 24g on od-1..od-4; the parallel repetitions ran the same command with --reps 1 (and, for SlushLarge, one worker count per call) on a set file holding the same entries; each row records its repetition and node

raw.location: dive evidence archive bucket (us-east-1), prefix release-perf/2026-11-18/ (archive shardN is node od-N, spotN is spot-N)

deviations: Repetitions were spread across nodes of one type to finish sooner: an on-demand shard node ran repetition 1 (and 2 on od-1, od-3 and od-4, and 3 on od-4), spot nodes ran the rest. A shard node's dive-bench was stopped once its last kept repetition was recorded; the run in progress at that moment was discarded, never recorded. Each row's runs_rep_node_wall_ms names the node of every repetition.

dive-bench's golden check compares raw TLC counts and does not read conformance/expected-divergences.toml. At one worker MCCRDT, VoteProof, MCKVsnap and SpanTreeRandom differ from the golden exactly as registered there; the record names the entry (registered_divergence). Generated counts at more than one worker are diagnostics only (ADR 0086).
Release binary built on one bench node and copied to the others (independent builds were not byte-identical); dive_binary_sha256 names the copied binary.

nodes.od-1..od-4: the four on-demand D1 large-shard nodes, each on its own shard's models after its D1 pass
nodes.spot-1..spot-5: five spot instances of the same type, AMI and bootstrap (scripts/aws/bench-node.sh), volume provisioned at 16000 IOPS and 1000 MiB/s, launched to run later repetitions in parallel; dive and dive-bench copied from the first node and checked by SHA-256 before timing

selection: The 48-model large class of the D1 record, less specifications/CheckpointCoordination/MCCheckpointCoordinationFailure.cfg: dive-bench needs a success golden, and that model's golden is a violation.

SlushLarge_with_D1_one_worker_time.note: D4's 1-worker SlushLarge runs stop at dive-bench's 3570 s time limit; D1 timed the same binary on the same host type at 6544.78 s to completion. Speed-ups against that time:
